reading.title: Word Endings That Name People and Events
reading.purpose: Learn how word endings turn action words into people, feelings, and gatherings.
paras: Look at the end of a long word, and you can often tell what job it does. Some endings turn an action word into the person who does it. Other endings turn an action into a feeling, a deal, or an event.

The endings -er and -or often name a doer. An explorer travels to new places to map rivers or caves. An inventor creates a brand-new tool for the first time. A swim instructor teaches beginners how to kick and float. A coin collector gathers old coins as a favorite hobby.

The ending -ment often names a feeling or the result of an action. You feel excitement, a strong and happy rush, right before a big trip. A funny puppet show brings amusement and makes the whole room laugh. When two friends shake hands on a shared promise, they have an agreement. At a clinic, a nurse gives careful treatment to help a scraped knee heal.
The ending -tion can name a group or a happy event. Shelves filled with seashells make a neat collection. When a neighborhood holds a block party with music and cake, everyone enjoys the celebration.
Spotting endings like -er, -or, -ment, and -tion makes long words easy to read.

choices: a funny puppet show that makes people laugh
a shared promise that two people say yes to
a shelf filled with seashells and old coins
a nurse helping a scraped knee heal quickly
qs.why: Paragraph 3 explains that when two friends shake hands on a shared promise, they have an agreement.

qs.q: Which sentence tells what an instructor does?
choices: An explorer travels to new places to map rivers or caves.
An inventor creates a brand-new tool for the first time.
A swim instructor teaches beginners how to kick and float.
A coin collector gathers old coins as a favorite hobby.
qs.why: This sentence shows the swim instructor teaching beginners a skill.

ev.text: A swim instructor teaches beginners how to kick and float.

qs.q: Omar has forty painted rocks lined up on a shelf in his bedroom. Which word from the reading names his group of rocks?
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says shelves filled with gathered items make a collection.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only swimmers and nurses need to know how long English words are built in books.
Word endings like -er, -or, -ment, and -tion help you read long words.
Collecting coins and seashells is much better than going to a block party.
Every action word in English can take the ending -tion at the very end.
qs.why: The reading explains what each group of endings means and closes by noting that spotting them makes long words easy to read.

a block party with music and cake
